title: NWB conversion needed three real fixes before trusting a number: dangling references (v1->v2), unreclaimed HDF5 space (v2->v3), and an H5Ocopy scale limit (v3->v4)

claims.statement: The first real conversion of sub-V198o_ses-230720_rec.nwb (v1 of scripts/convert_nwb_compressed.py, full 942s run against the real 83.96 GiB file) produced an output file that pynwb.NWBHDF5IO(...).read() cannot open.
claims.receipt: pynwb read attempt: KeyError "Unable to open object by token (address of object past end of allocation)" -- the canonical signature of a dangling HDF5 object reference. Root cause: v1 walked the source tree via visititems and copied attributes individually with `dst_obj.attrs[k] = v`; acquisition/probe_0_lfp/electrodes carries an h5py.Reference attribute (`table`) pointing at the shared electrodes DynamicTable -- 162 such reference-typed objects/attrs found in this file by scan. A raw h5py.Reference is only valid within the file it was read from; copying its value into a new file leaves an address that does not exist there.

claims.statement: v1's round-trip verification reported PASSED and every individual check it ran was factually correct -- it simply never exercised the object-reference graph pynwb depends on. The earlier session turn that reported 'VERIFICATION PASSED' was a true statement about a false sense of completeness, not a false statement.
claims.receipt: v1 verify_roundtrip compared only raw array bytes (LFP/MUAE/spike_train samples, units/electrodes ids, reconstructed timestamps) -- all 8 of those checks passed on the real file and still pass identically under v2. None of them touch h5py.Reference resolution, which is exactly the corrupted path.
claims.note: The general lesson, not specific to this script: byte-level round-trip equality is necessary but not sufficient for a structured format with internal cross-references. The format's own reader is the only complete check.

claims.statement: v2 copies the source tree via a single atomic h5py Group.copy(expand_refs=True) call on the whole root, rather than one call per top-level group. Verified on a synthetic fixture built specifically to contain a cross-top-level-group HDF5 reference (acquisition/probe_0_lfp/electrodes -> /electrodes), the exact pattern that broke v1.
claims.receipt: Two synthetic runs, 2026-08-08. First attempt (loop over src.keys(), each copied separately with expand_refs=True): reference resolved to /~obj_pointed_by_3211112, NOT /electrodes -- h5py's expand_refs treats a reference target outside the object currently being copied as external and duplicates it anonymously, since each top-level group was copied in a separate call and the reference's target group had not been established as 'the same object' yet. Second attempt (whole root copied in one call, landed under a temp group, then flattened via dst.move): reference resolved to /electrodes exactly, and target['id'] data-identical to the real copy at /electrodes.

claims.statement: The synthetic fixture used to verify the reference fix is itself not pynwb-readable, independent of any conversion -- confirmed by attempting to read the UNCONVERTED source fixture directly, which fails identically. The real pynwb check therefore had to run against the actual NWB file, not the synthetic one.
claims.receipt: pynwb.NWBHDF5IO(synthetic_source_path, 'r').read() -> ValueError: No data_type found for builder root, BEFORE any conversion step touches the file. The fixture lacks a /specifications group and NWB namespace schema; it was built only to exercise HDF5-level reference semantics, not full schema conformance.

claims.statement: v1's measured (corrupted-but-byte-accurate) conversion of the real file: 83.96 GiB -> 40.58 GiB, 2.07x, with convolved_spike_train kept but NOT compressed (verbatim copy, still 17.41 GiB / 43% of the output). This ratio is real for the transformations it performed, but the file itself is unusable due to the reference bug and the number will change under v2, which additionally compresses convolved_spike_train in place.
claims.receipt: src_bytes 90155431792, dst_bytes 43576422979 (log: /tmp/convert_log.txt). Per-dataset on-disk sizes measured via h5py Dataset.id.get_storage_size(): LFP 5.60+5.90 GiB (float32 logical 7.01 GiB each, ratio 1.25x/1.19x, consistent with the spec's own 1.22-1.23x gzip1+shuffle benchmark), MUAE 5.33+5.57 GiB (1.31x/1.26x), spike_train 8.68 GiB -> 0.10 GiB (86.8x, same direction as but below the spec's 179x on a possibly-different-density sample), convolved_spike_train 17.36 GiB logical, 17.41 GiB on disk, compression=None (untouched, as expected since v1's default path copies it verbatim).
claims.note: max_float32_err measured at 2.44e-4 on this file (vs the spec's own benchmark of 3.05e-05 on a different, smaller-range file) -- both are far below any plausible signal floor, but the two are not directly comparable without knowing this file's amplitude range; not yet checked here.

claims.statement: v4 (per-group copy + explicit reference repair + mandatory compaction) converted the real 83.96 GiB file to 29.68 GiB (2.83x), verified at three independent layers: raw h5py byte comparison against source, a full pynwb.NWBHDF5IO(...).read(), and a fresh (cache-cleared) jnwb.read() through this project own session loader with real epoch/unit/electrode extraction.
claims.receipt: src_bytes 90155431792, dst_bytes 31871792726 (log: scripts run 2026-08-08 23:xx, ~/tmp/convert_log_v4.txt). bloated_bytes 90155418932 -> compacted 31871792726, compaction_reclaimed_bytes 58283626206 (64.6% of the pre-compaction size was unreclaimed HDF5 free space -- confirms claim-atomic-root-copy-fails-at-real-scale sibling finding that compaction is not optional). pynwb read: 8 acquisition series, 317 units, no exception. jnwb.read() after deleting the stale artifacts/developer/.cache/sub-V198o_ses-230720_rec_*.pkl entries (first attempt was a FALSE PASS -- the cache keys only on filename stem, not path or content hash, so it silently served tables cached from an earlier read of the ORIGINAL file at a different path; caught before being reported): 186 stable_plus units, 2880 AAAB correct epochs, 256 electrodes, 256 lfp_channel_areas rows, log line confirms Cached (fresh write) not a cache hit. max_float32_err 2.4376e-04 on this file, same order of magnitude as the source-file-level check earlier (1.137e-04 on the same probe_0_lfp array via a separate byte-sample comparison).
claims.note: Also confirms convolved_spike_train recompression: kept (data loss NOT taken, per the load-bearing deviation from the spec), byte-exact, now under gzip1+shuffle rather than uncompressed.

claims.statement: The atomic whole-tree root-copy-with-expand_refs technique that fixed v1 (and that fixed the earlier compaction bloat) itself fails on the real 84 GiB post-churn file with RuntimeError: bad object header version number, while succeeding on synthetic fixtures up to ~2 GiB with the same structure. Replaced with per-top-level-group copy (no expand_refs) plus an explicit reference-resolution pass that repairs both attribute-valued references and the one dataset holding reference-typed CONTENT (general/extracellular_ephys/electrodes/group, an NWB DynamicTable column of per-row ElectrodeGroup references).
claims.receipt: v3 log: Step 1 (root-copy of the CLEAN, unchurned source) succeeded in 137.6s; Step 4 (root-copy of the SAME technique applied to the post-churn bloated file) failed with RuntimeError. Not reproduced on synthetic fixtures at 2 MB or ~2 GiB with matching chunked/filtered/reference-bearing structure -- a genuine HDF5 H5Ocopy+expand_refs scale/format limit, not a bug in how this script called it. v4 (per-group copy + _resolve_references) verified correct on: (a) the small reference-bearing fixture -- both an attribute reference AND a dataset-content reference array resolve to the correct target path; (b) the ~2 GiB fixture -- correct AND faster (1.8s structural copy + 1.0s compaction, vs the old atomic approach).
claims.note: Third distinct real bug found in three consecutive runs of the same script, each only visible at real file scale or against the real reference-bearing structure. Every fix was verified on a purpose-built synthetic fixture before being run against the 84 GiB real file again -- this is the discipline that kept each retry cheap (seconds to tens of seconds) rather than another 15-45 minute real-file loss.

claims.statement: Started converting the corpus one file at a time to reclaim disk space, smallest first, deleting each original only after full 3-layer verification. First cycle: sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec (the 22nd/uncatalogued session, actually the smallest at 19.59 GiB, smaller than the 83.96 GiB validation file) converted 19.59 -> 6.67 GiB (2.94x), verified (byte comparison, pynwb read, fresh cache-cleared jnwb.read: 354 stable_plus units, 720 AAAB epochs, 256 electrodes), original deleted. D: free space 894.7 -> 914.3 GiB, delta matches the deleted file size exactly.
claims.receipt: Log: bloated_bytes 23124427370, dst_bytes 7163964357, compaction_reclaimed_bytes 15960463013 (69% of pre-compaction size, consistent with the 64.6% reclaimed on the 84 GiB validation file). jnwb.read() log line confirmed "Cached... to disk cache" (fresh write, not the stale-cache false-pass pattern from the first file). Original at D:/nwb/omission/sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec.nwb deleted with explicit per-file user confirmation, per the confirmed campaign plan (convert smallest-first, delete only after verification passes, ask before each delete).

claims.statement: The corpus has at least three independent structural variants in LFP/MUAE path nesting and probe count, and they vary INDEPENDENTLY -- neither can be assumed from subject or from a previously-checked file. The hardcoded 4-path LFP_MUAE_PATHS tuple validated against V198o files silently matched nothing on sub-V182o_ses-260724, meaning that conversion would have skipped LFP/MUAE compression entirely with no warning had the run not separately crashed on an unrelated bug first.
claims.receipt: Structural audit 2026-08-09: V198o (230720, 230629) -- acquisition/probe_N_lfp/data, 2 probes, flat. V182o (260724) -- acquisition/probe_N_lfp/probe_N_lfp_data/data, 3 probes, one extra nesting level. C31o (230816) -- acquisition/probe_N_lfp/data, 3 probes, flat (same flat convention as V198o but 3 probes like V182o -- probe count and nesting are independent). Fixed by discovering LFP/MUAE paths via regex (probe_\d+_(?:lfp|muae))(?:/_data)?/data$, anchored to the two known shapes via backreference. A first draft of this regex (bare substring match) also matched the small electrodes-region-index dataset nested inside the LFP group and crashed on a chunk-rank mismatch -- caught on a synthetic fixture before touching real data.
claims.note: SPIKE_TRAIN_PATH and CONVOLVED_PATH remain hardcoded constants since they matched identically across all 3 subjects checked, but convert() now raises KeyError loudly if either is absent from a given session, rather than silently skipping as the old LFP/MUAE code did.

claims.statement: sub-V182o_ses-260724 already carries a starting_time+rate dataset alongside an explicit (redundant) timestamps array for some TimeSeries, copied verbatim by Step 1. Step 3 then crashed trying to create a second starting_time at the same location. Fixed by checking for a pre-existing starting_time before creating one: if present, reconstruct timestamps from it and compare against the array being collapsed -- if consistent (max abs err < 1e-6), drop the redundant timestamps array; if NOT consistent, keep both and record the mismatch rather than guessing which is authoritative.
claims.receipt: Real crash: ValueError: Unable to synchronously create dataset (name already exists) at acquisition/probe_0_lfp/probe_0_lfp_data/starting_time, after Step 1/2 completed successfully (139.4s, 11 references repaired). Verified on a synthetic fixture with both a CONSISTENT pre-existing starting_time (correctly: starting_time kept, timestamps dropped, err reported 0.0) and a DELIBERATELY INCONSISTENT one (correctly: both kept, err reported 1038.999, nothing silently discarded).
claims.note: The crashed v2-of-260724 run left a 61.7 GiB .bloated.tmp file on D: -- deleted immediately given the active disk-space constraint, before diagnosing the root cause.

claims.statement: sub-V182o_ses-260724 fails strict pynwb.NWBHDF5IO(...).read() on BOTH the raw source and the converted file, with an IDENTICAL ConstructError: general/devices/probeA stores description/manufacturer as 1-element object ndarrays instead of scalar strings, which pynwb Device.__init__ rejects. Verified byte-for-byte identical across every attribute on that object between source and converted file -- this is a pre-existing data-quality defect in the corpus, not something the converter introduced. The verify_roundtrip pynwb check was corrected: the bar is now does not parse WORSE than the source (fails identically or not at all), not parses cleanly -- the old strict-pass requirement would have blocked forever on any already-non-conformant session, which is not this scripts problem to fix.
claims.receipt: pynwb read attempted directly on D:/nwb/omission/sub-V182o_ses-260724.nwb (untouched original): same ConstructError, same GroupBuilder repr, same object_id 3e5a083a-4062-47c5-aaaa-fe269f9adc20. h5py attribute dump of general/devices/probeA on both files: description, manufacturer, namespace, neurodata_type, object_id all MATCH exactly. Despite this, jnwb.read() (this projects own loader, fresh cache) succeeds fully on the converted file: 194 stable_plus units, 1704 AAAB correct epochs, 288 electrodes -- jnwb evidently does not route through pynwbs strict Device construction for the fields this project actually uses, so the file is fully usable for real analysis despite failing strict NWB-schema validation.

claims.statement: sub-V182o_ses-260724 converted and verified: 57.46 GiB -> 20.77 GiB (2.77x), all 6 LFP/MUAE arrays correctly discovered and compressed (the bug this file exposed), 8 redundant timestamps arrays correctly dropped with zero inconsistency, byte comparisons pass, pynwb parses no worse than source, fresh jnwb.read() succeeds with real epoch/unit/electrode extraction.
claims.receipt: src_bytes 61695772798, dst_bytes 22297844417, compaction_reclaimed_bytes 39398122681 (63.9% of pre-compaction size, consistent with the 64-69% reclaimed on the two prior files). max_float32_err 6.099e-05.

claims.statement: Correct-trial counts (distinct trial_num with correct==1) verified for the 3 converted-and-still-present sessions. sub-V198o_ses-230720_rec: 960 trials, 12 rows/trial, IDENTICAL between the still-present original and the converted file (true before/after regression check). sub-V182o_ses-260724: 960 trials, 8 rows/trial (uniform, differs from V198o row count as expected given the known structural differences between subjects). sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec: only 220 distinct correct trials, with IRREGULAR rows/trial (145 trials x 17 rows, 75 trials x 15 rows) -- does not match the ~960 expectation.
claims.receipt: 230720 original: get_epochs(correct_only=True) -> 11520 rows, 960 distinct trial_num, rows/trial value_counts {12: 960}. 230720 converted: identical, 11520 rows, 960 trials, {12: 960}. 260724 converted: 7680 rows, 960 trials, {8: 960}. 230629 converted: 3590 rows, 220 trials, {17: 145, 15: 75}.

claims.statement: The 220-trial/irregular-row-count result for sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec is a property of the SOURCE recording, not something the conversion introduced. The converter never touches anything under intervals/ -- its transform patterns (LFP/MUAE data paths, SPIKE_TRAIN_PATH, CONVOLVED_PATH, and any 1D float dataset literally named timestamps) cannot match an intervals table, which uses start_time/stop_time columns, not timestamps. Confirmed no timestamps or starting_time dataset exists in this files intervals/omission_glo_passive group.
claims.receipt: h5py inspection of converted file: intervals/omission_glo_passive has no timestamps or starting_time key; trial_num and correct columns both shape (4163,) (raw event-row count, consistent with the 3590 correct-row subset found). Original for this session was already deleted (converted+verified+deleted in an earlier cycle this same session), so a direct before/after byte comparison is no longer possible -- this claim rests on structural reasoning about what the converter can touch, not a source-vs-converted diff.
claims.note: This is the same session flagged earlier (data-volume-layout-and-tfr-spec-transfer-20260808.json claim-22nd-session-not-in-either-inventory) as absent from both session_readiness.csv and nwb_catalog.json with no recorded reason. A 220-trial session with irregular per-trial structure, versus 960 uniform elsewhere, is a plausible explanation for that exclusion -- an anomalous or incomplete recording that failed some readiness gate. Worth investigating further before this session is used in any trial-count-sensitive analysis; it should NOT be assumed to behave like the other 21 sessions.

claims.statement: sub-V198o_ses-230721_rec converted and fully verified: 86.56 GiB -> 31.04 GiB (2.79x). Clean pynwb read (no pre-existing defect this time). jnwb.read() fresh: 190 stable_plus units, 256 electrodes. Correct trials: 960 distinct trial_num, uniform 12 rows/trial -- matches the 230720 pattern exactly, both members of the V198o structural family.
claims.receipt: src_bytes 92938616400, dst_bytes 33325288612, compaction_reclaimed_bytes 59613314584 (64.1% of pre-compaction size). max_float32_err 2.4386e-04. get_epochs(correct_only=True): 11520 rows, 960 trial_num, {12: 960}.

claims.statement: A FOURTH structural variant exists: sub-V182o_ses-260713 has 4 probes (not 2 or 3) AND an entirely EMPTY processing/ group -- no spike_train, no convolved_spike_train. It stores spikes only as units/spike_times ragged arrays (standard NWB), with no dense binned matrix. The loud KeyError guard added after the LFP/MUAE silent-skip incident correctly caught this rather than silently skipping, but its verdict was wrong: absence here is a legitimate structural variant, not an unrecognized convention.
claims.receipt: Run crashed at Step 2 with KeyError on processing/spike_train/spike_train_data/data after successfully discovering and listing all 8 LFP/MUAE arrays (probe_0..probe_3 x lfp/muae, nested convention). h5py inspection: processing/ keys == [] (empty); the only spike data is units/spike_times shape (17410546,) with units/spike_times_index shape (374,), plus spike_amplitudes. Probe count now observed at 2 (V198o), 3 (V182o_260724, C31o), and 4 (V182o_260713) -- so probe count varies WITHIN subject V182o, not just between subjects.
claims.note: Fixed by discriminating legitimate absence from unknown convention: if processing/ is empty, the datasets are genuinely absent -> record in absent_optional_datasets and proceed; if processing/ is NON-empty but the expected paths are missing, that IS an unrecognized convention -> still raise. Both branches verified on synthetic fixtures. This preserves the silent-skip protection the guard was added for while not failing on a real variant.

claims.statement: User granted standing authorization 2026-08-09 to delete each original NWB once its compressed copy exists, replacing the prior per-file confirmation. Applied policy: delete ONLY after that specific file passed full verification; never delete while its conversion is still in flight. First application: sub-V198o_ses-230720_rec original (83.96 GiB) deleted after a final pre-delete read-check of the converted copy.
claims.receipt: Pre-delete confirmation on D:/analysis/nwb_converted/sub-V198o_ses-230720_rec.nwb with cleared cache: jnwb.read() OK, 186 stable_plus units, 256 electrodes, 960 correct trials at uniform 12 rows/trial -- matching the values measured on the original before deletion. D: free 792.1 -> 775.8 GiB (net; three parallel bloated temps totalling ~315 GiB are concurrently on disk, which is why free space did not rise by the full 83.96).
claims.note: This session (230720) was the original validation file, kept deliberately longer than the others so its original could serve as the before/after reference for the correct-trial regression check. That check is complete (960 trials identical on both copies), so the original had no remaining purpose.

claims.statement: sub-V182o_ses-260722 converted and verified under 3-way parallel load: 105.41 GiB -> 38.61 GiB (2.73x). 8 LFP/MUAE arrays (4 probes, nested convention) discovered and compressed. 960 correct trials, uniform 8 rows/trial. Original deleted per standing authorization.
claims.receipt: elapsed_s 2404.3, compaction_reclaimed_bytes 71731521829 (65.0% of pre-compaction), max_float32_err 2.4412e-04, VERIFICATION PASSED (no FAIL lines). Fresh cache-cleared jnwb.read(): 122 stable_plus units, 512 electrodes, get_epochs(correct_only=True) -> 960 distinct trial_num at {8: 960}.

claims.statement: Three-way parallel conversion is CPU-bound, not I/O-bound, and yields roughly 2.2x aggregate throughput despite each individual file taking ~25% longer than it would alone. Parallelism is the correct strategy for this workload.
claims.receipt: Measured mid-run 2026-08-09 with 3 conversions active: CPU time as a fraction of wall time was 74%, 74%, 78% across the three python processes (i.e. each running near its single-threaded ceiling, not stalled on I/O); PhysicalDisk current queue length 1-2 (not saturated); ~2.3 of 24 cores in use. Serial baseline across 4 prior single-file runs: 0.0578 GiB/s (19.59/329s, 57.46/861s, 83.96/1717s, 86.56/1542s). Prediction from the 75%-efficiency model for 260722 (105.41 GiB): ~2430s; ACTUAL 2404s -- model confirmed to within 1%.
claims.note: Per-file latency worsens under parallelism while aggregate throughput improves -- these are different quantities and the per-file slowdown is not evidence against parallelizing. The real cost is that a crash strands one .bloated.tmp per in-flight file (up to ~315 GiB with 3 running), which must be cleaned up promptly under the disk constraint.

claims.statement: My correct-trial verification method was flawed: nunique(trial_num) UNDERCOUNTS in sessions where trial_num is reused across recording blocks. Corrected method is count(stimulus_number==1), since each trial contributes exactly one stimulus_number==1 event. On sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec this changes the count from 793 to 921. Re-checked all 13 converted sessions with the corrected method: 11 have exactly 960 and were correctly reported (nunique==stim1 for those, so trial_num is NOT reused there); only C31o_230816 (921) and V198o_230629 (220) deviate.
claims.receipt: sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec: 9210 correct rows, nunique(trial_num)=793, count(stimulus_number==1)=921, rows/10=921. stimulus_number value_counts shows exactly 921 each for values 1-5 plus 4605 NaN. Example trial_num 103.0 appears TWICE, at start_time 2114.3s and 12477.4s -- ~10363s apart, i.e. two separate recording blocks reusing the same trial numbering, not duplicated data. Full re-check table across all 13 converted sessions confirms 960 for the other 11.

claims.statement: sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec genuinely has 921 correct trials, not 960 -- short by 39 (4%). This is a property of the SOURCE recording, not a conversion artifact: the untouched original and the converted copy give byte-for-byte identical results (9210 rows, same 665x10 / 128x20 row split, same 921 stimulus_number==1 count).

CONVERTED -> identical on every one of those figures. C31o conversion itself: 142.05 GiB -> 51.38 GiB (2.77x), clean pynwb read (10 acquisition series, 357 units), VERIFICATION PASSED.
claims.note: No fifth structural variant in C31o -- 6 LFP/MUAE arrays (3 probes, flat convention), populated processing/, all paths discovered correctly. The 60-min runtime was Step 1 I/O contention (798s vs ~200s typical) under 3-way parallelism, not a structural problem. The remaining 6 C31o files should convert cleanly, but their trial counts must be checked with the CORRECTED method.

issues: v1's corrupted output file at D:/analysis/nwb_converted/sub-V198o_ses-230720_rec.nwb was deleted before v2's run, since it is not valid NWB and keeping it risks someone treating it as usable. The pynwb read check is now a REQUIRED part of verify_roundtrip going forward, not optional -- any future converter change must pass it before a ratio or timing number from that run is trusted.

max_float32_err on the real file (2.44e-4) has not been related to the file's actual signal range the way the spec did for its own benchmark file (rel ~2e-8 over range 1314). Should be computed once v2's real run lands, so the precision claim is stated relative to this file's own amplitude, not borrowed from a different session.

v3 left a 90 GiB .bloated.tmp file and an empty 8-byte partial .nwb on D: when it crashed mid-compaction -- cleaned up manually immediately given the disk-space constraint (D: has ~800-930 GiB free, budget is tight). Any future crash mid-run should be checked for the same leftover pattern before assuming disk state is clean.

A cache false-positive nearly became a false verification receipt: jnwb.read() on the converted file first returned a plausible-looking OK by silently hitting a stale disk cache keyed only on filename stem (artifacts/developer/.cache/), left over from reading the ORIGINAL file at a different path earlier the same session. Caught by noticing the log said "Loaded cached" rather than "Cached... to disk cache". The cache has no path/mtime/hash component -- worth fixing generally, since this could produce a false pass for ANY two files that happen to share a session-name stem.

This session -- sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec -- was the file whose absence from both session_readiness.csv and nwb_catalog.json was flagged unresolved earlier (data-volume-layout-and-tfr-spec-transfer-20260808.json claim-22nd-session-not-in-either-inventory). It has now been converted and its ORIGINAL deleted -- if that inventory omission was ever going to be investigated by re-examining the raw file, that window has closed for this session; only the converted copy remains.

sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec and sub-V198o_ses-230720_rec were converted BEFORE this LFP/MUAE path-discovery fix existed. Both happened to use the flat 2-probe convention the old hardcoded tuple matched, so their conversions were correct -- verified independently at the time via 3-layer checks. But this was not verified as a general property of the script at the time; it is now, retroactively, since those two files structural convention has since been confirmed to match what the old hardcoded paths assumed.

Compression ratio for sessions with an empty processing/ group will be LOWER than the 2.77-2.94x measured so far, because those sessions lack the two datasets that compress best (spike_train at ~87x due to 0.3% density, and the uncompressed convolved_spike_train). Such files are dominated by LFP/MUAE, which yields ~2x (float64->float32) x ~1.25x (gzip) after conversion. Do not treat the ~2.8x corpus figure as applying uniformly.
